To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have proposed a calculation method for flanges joints that takes into account all types of loading, including thermal transient loading.
the design of pressure vessel flanges should consider all the above-mentioned factors.
the current computing standards for flanges and bolts are insufficient to ensure the tightness and mechanical strength of the joint.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for the calculation of pressure vessel flanges and flange bolts in situations not considered by current international standards.
the design methods of the pressure vessels flange joints.
the development of a new calculation method for flanges and bolts in pressure vessels, which can be applied in all cases of loading of these components, including creep and fatigue.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the flange joint design method should be based on the calculation of the stresses in the flange and the bolts in all the possible loading situations, and not just on a single loading condition.
the calculation of a flange joint is not possible without the knowledge of the temperature of flange and bolts.

the current international standards do not take into consideration the most common situations of flange joints in service, namely: the temperature of the flanges and bolts are not equal; the flanges and the bolts are subjected to a sequence of blocks with variable normal stress; the flanges, the bolts and the gasket are subjected to a thermal transient loading; and, finally, creep stresses are not taken into account.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the design methods of flange joints in pressure vessels are based on the following principles: the flange joint is a mechanical structure that has to withstand a static load and a dynamic load (fatigue load), and the tightness of the joint is ensured by the gasket.
, in order to obtain an adequate design of the pressure vessel flange joints, the designer should take into account the temperature and the thermal transient load, as well as the fatigue loading.
the calculation methods of the current computing standards (EN 13445 4: 2009, PD 5500:2009) for flange joint strength and tightness are not complete and need to be improved.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the maximum allowable difference is a function of the type of flange joint and the material of flanges and gaskets, and it is also influenced by the type of bolt material.
the current computing standards are insufficient for the evaluation of the mechanical strength and tightness of flanges and flange joints.
the design method for flange joint should be completed with the calculation of the mechanical stresses and the thermal stresses in the flange and bolt.
